jobs.description:
仿真场景搭建与资产配置:基于 NVIDIA Isaac Sim、Newton(Palatial/MuJoCo)等仿真平台,负责数字孪生场景搭建、机器人(如双臂机械臂、复合移动机器人)及物体的物理/渲染属性(USD、MJCF、Mass、Inertia、Bounds、CoACD 碰撞分解)配置与优化。
 抓取与操纵逻辑开发:负责物体抓取(Grasp Pose)、逆运动学(IK)、接触物理(Contact/Friction/Restitution)以及状态机(State Machine)逻辑的编写与测试。
 行为脚本与任务规划:编写基于 Python 的自动化行为脚本(Harness/Task Pipeline),实现“接近-抓取-抬起-振动/扰动测试-放置”等复杂离散/连续行为动作的逻辑控制与闭环校验。
 验证与指标分析:构建仿真测评 Pipeline(Metrics System),输出抓取成功率、滑移量(Contact Slide)、接触力等评估数据,并基于测试结果反向迭代 IK 与 Grasp 参数。
 算法协同与交付:与具身智能(Embodied AI)算法团队合作,为强化学习(RL)、模仿学习(Imitation Learning)或大模型部署提供高保真、稳定高并发的仿真环境与数据集生成接口。
 Real2Sim 与 Demo 生成:将第一人称视角(egocentric)等各类数据转化为高质量的 real2sim2real 仿真,用于数据集生成与 Demo 制作。
requirements: 计算机、机器人学、自动化、机电一体化等相关专业,本科及以上学历。
1 年及以上具身智能(Embodied AI)、机械臂抓取操纵或机器人仿真相关行业工作经验。
项目经验须体现机械臂抓取、灵巧手或接触操纵(manipulation)方向;仅有导航/SLAM/无人机/自动驾驶仿真经验、无操作类项目者不匹配。
精通 NVIDIA Isaac Sim (Omniverse) 或 Newton / MuJoCo 仿真框架,熟悉 USD / MJCF 物理描述文件结构。
熟悉仿真物理引擎机制(刚体动力学、接触力学、碰撞网格分解、CCD等)。
精通 Python,具备扎实的数据结构与软件工程规范,能够熟练编写面向对象的复杂逻辑脚本与自动化框架。
熟悉机器人学基础(空间变换、正/逆运动学 IK、碰撞检测算法)。
熟悉 Linux 深度开发环境、Git 版本控制与虚拟环境管理(venv / conda)。
具备严谨的调试与测试思维,能够独立追踪解决物理穿透、发散、接触抖动等仿真异常现象。
5. 英语能口头与书面沟通,能阅读英文技术文档
有 Palatial Newton、Isaac Gym 或 Brax 等高性能/并行仿真器实际项目经验者优先。
熟悉 ROS / ROS 2,具备硬件真机(如 UR、Franka、Yam 机械臂)部署或仿真到真机(Sim2Real)经验者优先。

1、熟悉伺服产品应用场景,专注通用伺服驱动器控制算法研究和迭代。 
2、具备丰富的量产伺服产品算法调试、问题攻坚、性能优化实战经验,能够独立发现产品控制短板,输出优化方案并落地验证,持续提升伺服产品响应速度、控制精度及工况适配性,支持产品差异化竞争与高端化升级。 
3、负责伺服三环(位置环、速度环、电流)控制算法优化,针对超调、震荡、低速抖动、高速响应滞后、稳态误差大、负载适应性差等都有切实的落地改良方案。 
4、对参数自辨识、死区补偿、摩擦力补偿、间隙补偿、高频振动抑制、低频抖动消除、弱磁控制、抗负责扰动观测、自适应PID、前馈控制等高性能算法都有深刻的理解,并能独立完成设计、仿真、代码实现及整机调试。 
5、跟踪先进伺服控制技术,结合公司产品定位,将新技术转化为量产可用方案,推动产品性能迭代升级。 
任职资格: 
1、硕士及以上学历,3年以上伺服(永磁同步电机)控制算法开发经验。 
2、有伺服三环(位置、速度、电流)控制算法优化落地应用经验,对伺服常见问题如速度超调/震荡、低速抖动、响应滞后、鲁棒性差等有优化经验。 
3、具备丰富的量产伺服产品算法调试、问题攻坚、性能优化实战经验,能够独立发现产品控制短板,输出优化方案并落地验证,持续提升伺服产品跟踪精度和鲁棒性,支持产品差异化竞争与高端化升级。 
4、对伺服速度控制高性能算法如机械/电气参数辨识、扰动观测器、摩擦力补偿、间隙补偿、振动抑制(高频共振和末端残余振动)、PID参数自适应等有实际开发经验,能独立完成算法设计、仿真设计、代码实现和调试闭环。 
5、对伺服电流控制高性能算法如弱磁控制、MTPA、模型预测控制、电流解耦等高性能算法有深刻的理解,并能独立完成算法设计、仿真、代码实现及整机调试。 
6、有伺服驱动器产品量产化应用经验优先。 
7、具有较强的软件调试能力,具备一定抗压能力。

jobs.description:
1. 负责机器人及机械臂端侧软件系统的全流程开发、调试与迭代维护,保障实机运行的稳定性与作业执行效率。
2. 落地机械臂运动控制、任务调度及智能控制算法的开发与验证工作,持续优化机械臂在抓取、装配、插拔等复杂操作场景下的作业精度与抗干扰能力。 
3. 推进强化学习、模仿学习等前沿算法在机器人实体操作任务中的工程化落地,完成算法从仿真环境到真实机械臂的迁移适配与效果调优。 
4. 联动感知、硬件、算法团队完成机器人感知、控制、决策模块的系统集成与跨设备联调,打通从模型训练到实机执行的完整交付链路。 
5. 快速定位并解决机器人现场运行中出现的软件缺陷、控制偏差及算法适配问题,沉淀技术解决方案与工程化规范,提升团队研发效率。
requirements: 1.语言要求:交流熟练掌握粤语、英语
2. 硕士及以上学历,计算机、自动化、机器人、机械电子、控制工程等相关专业,具备扎实的控制理论与软件工程基础。
3. 熟练掌握Linux开发环境,具备Linux环境下软件模块开发、调试及复杂问题排查能力;精通Python或C++至少一门编程语言,能独立完成功能模块的编码实现与性能优化。
4. 掌握机械臂运动学、动力学与控制相关基础理论,具备机械臂实机开发或调试经验,有力控机械臂实际操作与应用经验者优先。
5. 熟悉深度强化学习与模仿学习相关算法原理,了解SAC、PPO等在线强化学习方法及IQL等离线强化学习方法,掌握Behavior Cloning、Diffusion Policy等模仿学习方案,具备相关算法实际项目落地经验。
6. 了解VLA等机器人智能决策控制方案,熟悉LLM大模型微调(LoRA、DPO等)相关技术,了解视觉、雷达、触觉传感器等机器人环境感知技术原理。
7. 熟练使用ROS/ROS 2、MoveIt等机器人开发框架,掌握PyTorch、Isaac Sim、Isaac Lab、MuJoCo等深度学习与仿真工具;有强化学习/模仿学习算法在真实机械臂上的部署调试经验,或VLA、具身智能、大模型与机器人结合相关项目经验者优先。

西湖交互机器科技(杭州)有限公司,孵化自西湖大学跨力学实验室(Beyond Mechanics with Societal Impact Lab),是国内物理 AI 与商用具身智能机器人领域的前沿科创企业。 区别于传统纯数据驱动的数字化人工智能,公司以力学客观规律作为算法底层约束,融合智能感知与实时决策算法,让实体智能设备适配复杂物理工况,实现高安全性、可解释化落地作业。 依托实验室顶尖科研积淀,公司聚焦力学仿真、柔性材料、柔性感知三大核心研发方向,已在柔性机器人、自然人机交互取得关键性技术突破与产业化进展,其柔性机械臂实现“刚柔并济”突破,打破传统刚性机器人瓶颈,可完成复杂操作,提升人机协作安全性与适配性,填补行业空白。 当前公司为B端用户打造高阶机器人产品矩阵及定制化解决方案,深度落地特种作业、工业、医疗、康养等垂类场景,推动科研成果规模化应用,致力于成为全球具身智能机器人领域的技术引领者与场景落地标杆。

jobs.description: 近年来,大型模型(包括大型语言模型(LLMs)、视觉-语言模型(VLMs)和扩散模型(DMs))的突破性进展,为高级感知、抽象推理和生成建模带来了前所未有的能力。这些进步为赋予机器人更类人的智能和适应性提供了变革性机遇。尽管取得了显著进展,当前的具身智能大模型在现实世界部署时仍面临诸多限制。一个主要挑战是它们难以泛化到新任务、未见物体和动态环境。这通常源于缺乏固有的常识性判断和对物理世界的精确理解,而这些对于应对物理现实的不可预测性至关重要 。因此,开发新一代具身智能大模型,能够自主学习、适应并以人类水平的熟练度、安全性和多功能性执行复杂的开放世界操作任务。 1. 围绕具身智能中的计算机视觉、机器人学、强化学习、自然语言等人工智能问题开展研究。 2. 推动具身智能领域的技术落地,研究机械臂、轮式机器人、人形机器人等具身智能机器人的运动/感知/控制/规划/交互算法,包括但不限于具身机器人的物体操纵、移动抓取、移动导航等算法和三维物体或场景建模理解等算法,实现室内外复杂场景下具身智能机器人自主任务执行。 3. 参与机器人领域相关多模态大模型的构建,负责具身机器人的复杂任务规划,主动环境感知理解与交互,技能学习与控制等前沿算法研究,研发具有感知-控制-规划能力的具身智能大模型。
requirements: 1. 具有机器人的控制、规划、感知算法的研究经验,熟悉深度学习,计算机视觉,多模态算法,机器人决策规划控制领域的前沿研究。 2. 极佳的工程实现能力,熟练掌握C/C++、Java、Python等至少一门语言。 3. 具备较强学习能力,对新事物保有好奇心,并能快速适应新环境;良好的沟通能力和团队协同能力;能与他人合作,共同完成目标;对所在领域有热情,不惧困难与挑战,善于独立思考并反思总结。 4. 加分项: 1)有ACM/NOI/IOI、Kaggle、国内外数学大赛、机器学习、深度学习相关竞赛获奖者优先。 2)在国际知名期刊或会议(NeurIPS, ICML, ICLR,ICRA,IROS,CoRL,RSS,CVPR,ICCV,ECCV等)上发表过高水平论文者优先。 3)有多轴机械臂、足式机器人等机器人平台算法研发及工程经验者优先。

jobs.description:
一、产业大模型日常运维 
1. 负责企业产业大模型运行监控、性能优化、异常排查、日志分析、权限配置和版本管理,保障模型稳定、高效、安全运行。 
2. 完成数据清洗、数据标注、知识库更新、语料迭代、提示词维护等基础运维工作,持续提升模型效果与响应质量。 
3. 组织第三方交付成果的测试验收、问题整改、上线发布和效果复盘,推动问题闭环和版本持续优化。 
二、模型二次开发与功能迭代 
1. 根据生产、销售、技术、质量、设备、经营管理等需求,对第三方搭建的产业大模型进行二次开发、接口改造和功能扩展。 
2. 参与Prompt工程、工作流编排、RAG知识库构建、模型微调和效果调优,提升模型在行业场景中的准确率和实用性。 
3. 开展AI应用脚本开发、接口调用、页面配置和简单后端开发,提高系统适配性和交付效率。 
三、AI应用落地与业务对接 
1. 推动大模型在生产调度、质量管控、成本核算、设备运维、客户技术服务、经营分析等场景落地应用。 
2. 对接各业务部门,梳理AI需求,输出可落地的AI应用方案、功能原型、实施计划及评价指标。 
3. 协同业务部门梳理流程、标准和知识规则,推动AI能力嵌入现有管理流程和业务系统。 
四、系统集成与接口开发 
1. 负责AI大模型与ERP、MES、WMS、OA、设备物联网平台等系统的接口对接、数据互通和联调测试。 
2. 编写接口文档、部署说明、运维手册和操作指引,形成标准化AI应用交付流程。 
3. 配合完成日志管理、访问控制、备份恢复和运行巡检,提升系统可靠性和可维护性。 
五、AI项目管理与成果沉淀 
1. 跟进AI项目进度,协调第三方厂商、内部IT和业务部门完成需求确认、开发联调、测试验收和正式上线。 
2. 建立应用台账、案例库和数据指标看板,沉淀AI场景、优化经验和复用组件,逐步形成公司内部AI能力体系。 
3. 开展用户培训、推广辅导和使用支持,提升员工使用率、应用覆盖率和实际业务价值。 
六、安全与合规管理 
1. 负责模型数据安全、权限管理、敏感信息脱敏和合规审查,确保AI应用符合公司信息安全要求。 
2. 对不符合业务需求、数据质量或安全规范的模型方案和上线版本提出整改建议或暂缓上线建议。 
3. 完成上级交办的其他与AI应用建设、运维和推广相关工作。
requirements: 1、本科及以上学历,计算机科学与技术、软件工程、人工智能、数据科学与大数据技术、自动化、电子信息工程、数学与应用数学、统计学等相关专业;物联网工程、智能制造、工业工程、通信工程等专业优秀者亦可。
2、2年以上AI应用开发、大模型运维、NLP/机器学习项目相关经验,3年以上优先;具有制造业、工业互联网、装备制造、信息化建设项目经验者优先;具备知识库建设、系统接口集成、流程编排、二次开发或项目交付经验者优先。

(1). 国家职称/软考类:信息系统项目管理师、系统集成项目管理工程师、软件设计师、网络工程师等。
(2). 人工智能/职业技能类:人工智能工程师、人工智能训练师、人工智能应用工程师、生成式人工智能技术应用类证书等。
(3). 云与平台认证类:阿里云、华为云、腾讯云、百度智能云等AI应用开发、模型训练、云计算或大数据相关认证。
(4). 其他相关证书:TensorFlow/PyTorch开发、MLOps/DevOps、数据分析、信息安全、PMP等相关认证。
(5). 持有助理工程师、工程师或高级工程师职称者优先。

杭州宇泛智能科技股份有限公司成立于2014年3月,是国家专精特新重点“小巨人”企业、国家高新技术企业、浙江省科技小巨人企业、余杭区准独角兽企业,2020-2024年连续5年认定为杭州市准独角兽企业。

宇泛注重技术创新,拥有浙江省重点企业研究院,曾入选工信部《2024年人工智能赋能新型工业化典型应用案例》,工信部《2021年人工智能产业创新任务揭榜挂帅》揭榜优胜单位,杭州市《2022年人工智能重大科技创新项目》牵头单位,浙江省《2023年“尖兵”“领雁”研发攻关计划》第一参与单位。截至目前,公司已获得有效知识产权343项,其中软著184项 ,发明专利51项,外观设计专利71项,实用新型专利37项;作为主要起草单位主持参与制定已发布国家标准3项,团体标准9项。相关产品和方案迭代至今已在动态人脸识别领域和数智建造领域占据重要地位,获2022年浙江省科学技术进步奖三等奖、2023年中国自动化学会科技进步二等奖、浙江省首版次软件产品、省级工业新产品、杭州市优质产品等多项荣誉。

公司于2015年研发业界首批嵌入式动态人脸识别智能终端,2021年业界首创塔机多合一辅助驾驶装备,至今覆盖多模态视觉感知与身份核验终端、场景智能相机、“软定义”边缘智能安全网关、高危工程机械辅助驾驶装置等超400多款硬件。2017年发布业界领先的人工智能物联网AIoT产业中台,并以AIoT中台为承载,聚合产业链上下游软硬件生态合作伙伴,联合共建面向智能建造、智慧社区、智慧楼宇等智慧城市细胞单元场景数智化解决方案。截止目前,第三方开发企业数量超2万家,拥有近4亿终端注册用户,具有良好的生态效益。
公司自建全国所有和海外近70个国家渠道。在智能建造领域,大规模应用于中国建筑、中国电建、浙建集团等央国企。在智慧工地实名制领域,全国市占率超70%,市占率第一。在智慧社区领域,是移动、联想、电信三大运营商的主要产品供应商,在数万小区展开落地应用。在智慧园区/楼宇领域,构建人、车、资产、安防、能源等一体化管理系统,在当虹科技总部大楼、河南龙湖金融中心等标志性场景落地解决方案。

requirements: 1、硕士及以上学历,机器人、自动化、计算机、人工智能、控制、机械等相关专业;

导航定位:SLAM、状态估计、点云配准、路径规划、ROS2 / Nav2;
视觉伺服机械臂控制:正逆运动学、轨迹规划、PID 控制、ROS2 / MoveIt2;
具身智能:深度学习、Transformer、VLM / VLA、模仿学习或强化学习。

使用过 Gazebo、MuJoCo、Isaac Sim、Isaac Lab 等机器人仿真环境,有 Sim2Real 相关实践经验;
有真实机器人、无人车、无人机或机械臂的传感器接入、数据采集、标定、控制及系统联调经验。

8. 配合完成其他与课程教学、技术答疑相关的工作。

1. 具备一定的C语言基础,能够看懂和修改基础代码。 
2. 具备一定的Python基础,能够完成简单程序编写和基础报错排查。 
3. 了解数字电路、模拟电路相关基础知识。 
4. 能够看懂基础电路图、模块接线图和引脚说明。 
5. 有焊接、接线、电子元器件安装或硬件调试经验。

jobs.description:
工作职责 
1.技术路线与架构规划 
定义物流人形 VLA 整体技术架构:视觉感知、多模态理解、自然语言任务指令解析、动作生成、全身运动控制、抓取操作闭环;制定 1-3 年物流场景 VLA 技术演进路线。 
2.VLA 模型研发与场景适配 
主导物流专属 VLA 大模型预训练、微调、RLHF / 模仿学习、强化学习落地;针对料箱、纸箱、包裹、不规则货物、货架、托盘做物体识别、姿态估计、6DoF 抓取、场景语义理解、环境动态避障。 
3.物流数据集与仿真平台建设 
搭建物流人形机器人多模态数据集采集、标注、清洗、迭代闭环;基于 Isaac Sim/MuJoCo 搭建物流仓储仿真环境,推进 Sim2Real 迁移,大幅降低真机调试成本。 
4.真机落地与工程化 
主导 VLA 算法与人形本体、运动控制、整机固件、调度系统、仓储 WMS/AGV 系统联调;解决真实仓储光照变化、货物堆叠遮挡、地面不平整、人员混行等复杂工况鲁棒性问题,保证高频稳定作业。 
5.团队管理与跨部门协同 
组建并管理 VLA / 具身智能算法团队,负责招聘、技术攻关、里程碑交付;对接产品、硬件、结构、电控、产线、物流客户,定义场景需求、算法指标、交付标准。 
6.前沿技术引入与专利壁垒 
跟进世界模型、具身大模型、端到端 VLA、扩散策略等前沿,快速落地到物流作业场景;主导技术专利、软著、顶会论文布局。
requirements: 1.硬性要求:计算机科学、人工智能、机器人学、自动化、控制工程、计算机视觉等相关专业博士学历(海外顶尖高校博士优先)。
2.工作经验:3 年以上 VLA / 具身智能 / 人形机器人算法研发经验(含博士期间课题研究及博士后经历),有物流仓储、分拣、抓取、码垛、工业搬运场景算法落地经验者优先。
3.博士期间深耕 VLA 多模态学习、具身智能、强化学习 / 模仿学习等方向,有相关顶会(NeurIPS/ICML/ICRA/IROS/CVPR)论文发表或核心专利产出;
4.精通视觉 - 语言 - 动作多模态架构,熟悉 OpenVLA/RT-2/GR00T/π?等主流人形 VLA 框架,熟练运用 PyTorch/TensorFlow 进行大模型微调与优化;
5.精通机器人 3D 视觉技术(点云处理、深度估计、6DoF 姿态估计、物体检测分割),熟悉 ROS/ROS2、Isaac Sim/MuJoCo 仿真平台及真机部署全流程;
6.具备扎实的数学建模与算法推导能力,能独立攻克物流场景下 VLA 核心技术难题(如杂乱货物抓取、动态避障、Sim2Real 迁移)。
7.核心素质:强技术领导力与项目管理能力,能带领团队完成场景化落地指标;结果导向,具备跨部门(硬件、产品、客户)高效沟通能力;对人形机器人物流场景商业化有深刻理解与执着追求。
博士期间课题聚焦人形机器人或物流机器人相关方向;
有大规模物流机器人多模态数据集构建经验;
主导过物流场景人形机器人 / VLA 算法从原型到量产落地项目。
职位类别:计算机软、硬件/互联网/IT
有怡科技(Hfun?Tech)是一家专注通用具身智能机器人全栈研发的硬科技企业,前身北京有怡科技 2024 年在北京创立,2025 年落户浙江金华金义新区,为金华首家人形机器人产业化项目,获得地方政府基金投资。
公司由航天一院副首席科学家刘轶博士创立,核心团队来自航天一院、小鹏机器人、北理工、浙大等科研院所与头部企业,拥有十余年足式、人形机器人研发积累,曾参与国家 863 四足液压机器人项目,具备运动控制、整机硬件、3D 视觉、具身 AI 完整自研能力。
公司提出“本质人形、定向通用”产品理念,不片面追求外观拟人,聚焦机器人实际作业能力,采用腿臂复用模块化统一硬件平台,一套机体可切换人形、轮式、四足多种形态,降低多场景定制成本。
核心产品矩阵覆盖:T01 可变形本质人形机器人、GEN?HM01 全尺寸人形机器人、IND?HW03 轮式双臂作业机器人、四足特种机器人,同时提供教育开发套件与定制化机器人技术服务。
业务面向 B 端市场,落地智慧仓储物流、工业巡检、半导体新能源工厂、电力特种救援、文旅展厅导览、科研教育等场景,与京东等产业伙伴开展场景联合落地,致力于打造好用、易用、可规模化部署的通用机器人产品,推动具身智能产业真实落地。

| 我们正在基于可交互的 3D 仿真场景研发面向具身智能的世界模型。该岗位重点研究机器人动作与环境状态变化之间的关系,使模型能够从视觉、语言、机器人状态和动作序列中学习环境动力学,预测未来观测与状态,并服务于机器人规划、策略学习、数据生成和仿真到现实迁移。该岗位不是单纯的视频生成或 3D 场景制作岗位。候选人需要关注模型是否理解动作因果、物体持久性、空间关系、接触与交互结果,并建立能够衡量这些能力的训练和评测方法。## 工作职责- 基于厨房、客厅、商店等可交互 3D 仿真场景,构建世界模型训练与评测 pipeline。- 研究 action-conditioned video prediction、latent dynamics model、state-space model、video diffusion 和 autoregressive world model 等方法。- 融合 RGB、深度、点云、语义、机器人本体状态、动作、语言指令和物体状态等多模态信息。- 训练模型预测未来图像、3D 状态、物体轨迹、接触事件、奖励、成功概率或终止状态。- 利用仿真器生成大规模、可控且带有完整 ground truth 的交互轨迹,包括成功、失败、扰动和反事实数据。- 研究具有 3D 一致性、时间一致性、物体持久性和长时序记忆能力的世界表示。- 将世界模型用于机器人行为想象、model predictive control、策略规划、数据增强、奖励建模或策略预训练。- 设计世界模型 benchmark,评估视觉质量之外的动作可控性、动力学准确性、空间一致性、长期预测和下游任务收益。- 分析模型在遮挡、碰撞、物体状态变化、未见场景和未见动作组合上的失败模式与泛化能力。- 开发分布式训练、数据加载、实验管理、模型评测和可视化工具,提高研究迭代效率。- 与 3D 资产工程师协作扩展视觉与物体多样性,与机器人仿真工程师协作定义交互数据、状态标签和评测任务。- 跟踪并复现世界模型、视频生成、具身智能和 model-based reinforcement learning 的前沿工作,参与论文与开源项目。##
requirements: - 熟悉 Python 和 PyTorch,能够独立完成模型训练、数据处理、实验设计和结果分析。- 理解 transformer、diffusion model、flow matching、VAE 或其他生成模型的基本原理。- 理解序列建模、表示学习、条件生成或动力学建模中的至少一个方向。- 具备机器人学习或 3D 视觉基础,理解观测、状态、动作、轨迹、坐标系和相机等概念。- 能够将研究问题转化为明确的数据协议、模型目标、消融实验和量化评测指标。- 具备较强的论文阅读、模型复现、工程调试和独立研究能力。## 加分项- 有 world model、video prediction、video generation、model-based RL、imagination-based planning 或 neural simulator 相关经验。- 熟悉 Dreamer、TD-MPC、MuZero、V-JEPA、Genie、GAIA 或同类世界模型工作。- 熟悉 Diffusion Transformer、Video Transformer、state-space model、tokeni

4、负责算法从仿真到实机的迁移部署,开发在线动力学参数辨识与自适应校准方案,解决 sim2real gap 问题,保障真机运行的实时性与稳定性。 
5、建立算法鲁棒性评估机制,通过扰动测试验证运动策略在真实场景中的可靠性。

| 我们正在建设面向具身智能的仿真训练与真实场景执行系统。该岗位的最终目标不是只在仿真中获得较高成功率,而是让机器人进入真实的商店、客厅、厨房等场景,安全、稳定地完成导航、抓取、放置、整理和人与机器人协作等任务。该岗位负责打通从仿真场景、任务与数据构建,到策略训练、真机集成、现场调试和真实任务评测的完整链路。候选人需要具备良好的机器人系统与 Python 工程能力,能够定位感知、规划、控制、通信、硬件和环境之间的系统性问题,并对机器人在真实场景中的最终执行结果负责。## 工作职责- 在 RoboCasa、MuJoCo、Isaac Sim、SAPIEN、ManiSkill、robosuite 或其他平台中搭建机器人仿真场景。- 将 3D 资产转换并配置为 USD、URDF、MJCF 等仿真格式,完成尺度、坐标系、碰撞体、质量、摩擦力、关节和物理属性设置。- 根据真实商店、客厅、厨房等目标环境构建数字化场景,配置机器人、相机、光照、传感器和可操作物体,并控制仿真与实景之间的关键差异。- 设计具身智能任务,明确 instruction、initial state、action space、success condition、failure condition、reset distribution 和 benchmark split。- 为模仿学习、强化学习、Diffusion Policy、ACT、VLA 和 LeRobot 等训练流程生成、清洗和管理轨迹数据。- 将仿真或数据训练得到的策略部署到真实机器人,完成模型转换、推理服务、机器人接口、传感器接入和控制链路集成。- 在真实场景中完成机器人标定、定位、导航、抓取与操作调试,包括相机内外参、手眼标定、坐标系、末端执行器和动作精度校准。- 设计并实施 sim-to-real 方案,包括域随机化、系统辨识、真实数据回采、策略微调和仿真参数校准。- 组织真实机器人任务测试,建立现场部署、任务初始化、失败恢复、人工接管、日志回传和重复实验流程。- 分析真机失败案例,区分感知、规划、控制、通信、策略、硬件和场景因素,并推动问题闭环。- 为真实环境中的人员、设备和物体制定安全约束,落实速度与力限制、碰撞保护、急停、工作空间限制和异常降级机制。- 开发自动化场景与任务检查工具,检测穿模、碰撞体错误、动力学异常、不可达、不可抓取、任务无法重置和成功判定失效等问题。- 建立贯通仿真与真机的可复现训练和评测 pipeline,对比成功率、碰撞率、恢复率、任务耗时、泛化能力和 sim-to-real gap。- 设计场景、物体、初始状态和语言指令的随机化方案,并控制训练集、验证集和测试集之间的泛化难度。- 使用 Codex 等 Agent 工具辅助代码开发、批量实验、数据清洗、结果分析和失败案例归因。- 与生成式 AI Agent 与 3D 资产工程师协作定义资产接入标准,与世界模型研究工程师协作定义交互数据和策略接口。- 参与机器人学习、sim-to-real、真实场景部署和 benchmark 方向的创新研究与论文工作。##
requirements: - 熟悉 Python,能够独立完成仿真环境、数据处理、实验脚本和自动化工具开发。- 理解机器人学基础,包括坐标变换、位姿、运动学、轨迹、碰撞检测、传感器和控制等概念。- 具有真实机器人开发或实验经验,能够进行设备连接、标定、动作调试、日志分析和故障排查。- 熟悉 Linux 环境,能够使用 ROS 或 ROS 2 完成机器人、传感器和算法模块之间的集成。- 了解机器人操作、导航、模仿学习或强化学习中的至少一个方向,并理解从模型输出到真实机器人动作执行的完整链路。- 理解 mesh、碰撞体、质量、摩擦力、关节、材质、相机和尺度等仿真资产概念。- 能够定义清晰、可执行、可自动评测的机器人任务,并将同一任务协议落实到仿真和真实环境。- 具备较强的问题拆解、现场调试和工程执行能力,愿意参与真实场景搭建、真机实验和迭代部署。## 加分项- 熟悉 MuJoCo、RoboCasa、robosuite、Isaac Sim、SAPIEN、ManiSkill 或 Habitat 中的一个或多个平台。- 熟悉 imitation learning、reinforcement learning、Diffus

articles.title: TanCRAFT: Context-Reasoned Anticipatory Feedback for Assembly Tasks
articles.summary: Preventing human error in physical assembly tasks requires assistance systems that can intervene before mistakes are made. This is especially challenging in settings where users are free to choose the construction order and correctness depends on the evolving assembly rather than a fixed next step. We present TanCRAFT, a four-stage real-time predictive assistance system that tracks the scene state, reasons about the current partial assembly, forecasts the near-future motion of manipulated pieces, and intervenes when the predicted placement is incompatible with the target. We instantiate our framework and confirm its effectiveness in a controlled tangram assembly task through offline benchmarks and a within-subject user study. Our findings show that the predictive feedback significantly reduces mistakes relative to unguided and reactive sessions, while yielding the lowest mean perceived workload and shortest mean completion time. articles.title: From Prediction to Action: Learning Physical Context for Deformable Linear Object Manipulation
articles.summary: A representation that accurately predicts a deformable object's response is not necessarily the one most useful for choosing manipulation actions. We study this distinction between predictive utility and decision utility in planar single-grasp shape control of Deformable Linear Objects (DLOs). As a common decision backbone, we introduce Geometry-Pointer-Flow (GPF), a geometry-grounded policy that separates grasp-location selection from grasp-conditioned motion generation. Its geometry-only variant reduces one-step executed shape error by 32.8% relative to a DLO-specific diffusion policy, while using 18.7 times fewer parameters and achieving approximately 193 times faster inference. On this backbone, we compare physical context represented by ground-truth parameters, estimated parameters, and learned interaction-history representations, for both forward prediction and executed control. articles.title: Elastic-WAM: Adaptive Spatiotemporal Imagination for Efficient Robot Control
articles.summary: World-Action Models improve robot control by predicting future visual dynamics, but iterative video denoising incurs substantial inference overhead. Recent approaches reduce this cost through partial future denoising, yet typically rely on fixed refinement budgets. Our empirical observations reveal that preferred refinement depths vary across tasks and states, while different future regions exhibit varying relevance to action generation. Motivated by these findings, we propose Elastic-WAM, which adaptively allocates world refinement computation across temporal denoising time and spatial future space. A unified spatiotemporal refinement demand field governs when to stop world refinement, how far to advance each denoising step, and which regions to refresh. articles.title: Personalized Affective Perception via Continual Learning in Human-Agent Negotiation
articles.summary: Self-interested intelligent agents that negotiate with humans should interpret nonverbal expressions and adapt their behavior accordingly. However, generic facial-affect models degrade across individuals and contexts, creating a generalization gap. We introduce an affect-adaptive negotiation strategy that incorporates Continual Learning with Imagination for Facial Expression Recognition (CLIFER) to personalize valence-arousal perception in real time. Differential feedback converts changes in valence-arousal direction and intensity into adjustments of the agent's target utility. An asynchronous architecture updates CLIFER in the background during live interaction. articles.title: Koopman Model-Based Reinforcement Learning
articles.summary: We propose a Koopman model-based reinforcement learning (K-MBRL) algorithm for controlling nonlinear robotic systems with unknown dynamics. The K-MBRL learns a control policy by minimizing an approximate policy objective that combines the analytical immediate cost with an estimate of the future cost evaluated at the one-step predicted state. To this end, we develop a stochastic Koopman operator-based learning method to approximate the unknown nonlinear dynamics in a linear representation, while a critic function estimates the remaining future cost. This formulation offers two key advantages. First, the linear Koopman dynamics simplify the model-dependent policy gradient computation to a constant matrix product, enabling computationally efficient policy improvement. articles.title: LEASH: Stay Safe in Agentic Robotics
articles.summary: Foundation models such as GPT and Claude have shown strong capabilities in spatial understanding and embodied intelligence. These advances make agentic robotics a promising path toward artificial general intelligence in robotics. However, we find that using foundation models to control robots poses serious safety risks, and comprehensive safety evaluation is still lacking. We introduce RoboRisk, a comprehensive benchmark for evaluating safety in agentic robotics. Its 92 simulated tasks and 13 physical-robot tasks fall into five categories: Task-level Refusal (T), Plan Repair (P), Execution-time Hazard (E), Injection (I), and Sequential Memory (S). Prior benchmarks cover at most two of these categories, and several evaluate only text outputs. In contrast, RoboRisk covers all five and executes every task in closed loop. articles.title: Model-Free Runtime Measurement of Task-Relevant Information
articles.summary: Autonomous systems increasingly monitor physical kinematics, environmental states and task completion outcomes. While existing work provides methods to plan information seeking actions and interpret acquired observations, current approaches do not monitor whether the live process of information gathering is functioning properly. Consequently, such systems can remain operationally active without resolving outstanding mission requirements. To address this limitation, we introduce Acquisition-State Telemetry (AST), a model free architecture that evaluates ongoing information acquisition from observable evidence relative to declared task requirements. articles.title: DexSeed: Expanding Human Hand-Object Interactions into Robot Demonstrations for Dexterous Policy Learning
articles.summary: We study how to generate diverse, physically executable robot demonstrations for dexterous vision-language-action (VLA) learning. Existing demonstration-generation methods typically rely on costly teleoperated examples. Meanwhile, human hand--object datasets provide a reusable source, but existing transfer methods mainly reproduce given interactions. Turning these interactions into VLA training data further requires coverage of different objects and manipulation locations, together with executable arm and finger actions, and visual observations. To achieve this, we present DexSeed, a framework for low-cost generation of dexterous robot data from human hand--object interactions. Our key idea is to expand human sequences while preserving their grasps and realizing the resulting motions under arm-tracking dynamics in physics simulation. articles.title: LaST0.5: A Generalist World Action Model with Interaction-Centric Latent Reasoning
articles.summary: World Action Models (WAMs) have recently emerged as a promising paradigm for robotic manipulation, endowing policies with strong capabilities for modeling temporal and physical dynamics. Existing WAMs, encompassing both video-first action prediction and joint video-action modeling, directly transfer global physical representations from world models to action generation. However, global scene representations may underemphasize local robot-object interactions, creating a mismatch between representations optimized for world evolution and those required for manipulation. To bridge this gap, we propose LaST0.5, a novel WAM that introduces an interaction-centric physical representation between world modeling and action generation. Specifically, LaST0.5 learns a compact interaction-centric latent space under the supervision of visual interaction cues between the robot and the environment. articles.title: Optimization-Based Path Planning for Industrial Manipulators: Experimental Validation in Additive Manufacturing
articles.summary: Robotic additive manufacturing requires joint paths that reconcile robot feasibility with process-specific geometry. We develop an offline optimization-based path planner that combines joint-path regularity and self-collision penalties with process costs and constraints, so that a new process enters through its own reference, residuals, and tolerances. Full-path and boundary-coupled chunked optimization handle references of different lengths. Iterative Weight Tuning (IWT) determines the cost weights from the gaps between Key Performance Indicators (KPIs) and their targets. In carbon-fiber winding and robotic 3D printing, the planned paths meet the geometric tolerances and all KPI targets, and both paths are executed on a UR10e, without extrusion for printing, with joint-level tracking recorded during execution.

articles.title: ReACT: Reflection-Consistent Modulation and Cross-Load Consistency for Humanoid Velocity Tracking Under Asymmetric Loads
articles.summary: In recent years, humanoid loco-manipulation has progressed to whole-body grasping, lifting, and transport. A basic requirement underlying these tasks is carrying the object to its destination, which depends on the locomotion controller accurately executing velocity commands from the navigation policy. However, carrying an object in one hand introduces a persistent asymmetric upper-body load that can degrade velocity tracking. Persistent tracking biases can accumulate into position and heading deviations, increasing the risk of collisions and navigation failure. To address this problem, we present ReACT, a framework for accurate velocity tracking under asymmetric upper-body loads. articles.title: Game-Enhanced Embodied Learning with Event and Foresight Pretraining
articles.summary: Human gameplay supplies paired observations, actions, and visual consequences that can supplement robot-policy training. We study event-and-foresight pretraining for InternVLA-A1.5, combining recorded keyboard/mouse event prediction with history-conditioned visual supervision through a frozen video model. Coverage-preserving anchor selection constructs one-second targets, and an attention mask prevents teacher-forced future actions from entering foresight queries. The selected corpus contains 394 recordings across 20 games, with 223.36 hours of recorded timestamp span and 2,072,084 training anchors. After 12,400 game-pretraining updates, we compare the resulting initialization with the public base under the same suite-specific robot fine-tuning protocol. articles.summary: This work presents the 2nd-place solution (Team IF1001) to the 2026 BEHAVIOR Challenge, which evaluates mobile manipulation across 100 household tasks. During inference, we apply a separate progress estimator to supply task-progress context, and use task- and progress-conditioned routing to select a task-group or skill-specific policy, complemented by action-candidate aggregation, rolling inpainting, and task-specific temporal and gripper control. articles.title: Camera equalisation of an 11.5x drop in environmental illuminance: four imitation-learning policies on an SO-101 arm
articles.summary: Real-robot benchmarks of learned visuomotor policies often record room illuminance as the lighting condition. We show that, on a typical low-cost rig, room light and image light can be almost unrelated. Four imitation-learning policies (ACT, SmolVLA, Diffusion Policy and pi0.5) were trained on the same 50 demonstrations of a pick-and-place task on an SO-101 arm. Each was run for ten rollouts at about 520 lux and again at about 45 lux, an 11.5x reduction. Success was 20/40 in normal light and 19/40 in low light: a change of -2.5 percentage points (95% CI -23 to +19), with no evidence that the policies differed in sensitivity (interaction p = 0.86). The recorded video shows why: mean image brightness was only 3% lower in low light on the front camera and 19% lower on the wrist camera. A great gap in adaptivity, flexibility, and dexterity still exists between intelligent robots, whether they are made of rigid or (partially) compliant components, and their naturally evolved animal and vegetal counterparts. One reason could be of `paradigm' nature. articles.title: CIALLO: Learning Shared Intent Representations for Cross-Embodiment Manipulation
articles.summary: Robot demonstrations contain reusable manipulation knowledge, but transferring this knowledge across embodiments requires representations that bridge differences in control interfaces. Action reconstruction alone does not ensure that similar behaviors across robots share a representation. An embodiment-conditioned decoder maps this intent back to robot-specific actions, allowing a shared representation to support different control interfaces. articles.title: A computational framework for understanding embodied plans
articles.summary: Reasoning about people's plans and goals based on their actions is fundamental to human social interaction and essential for cooperative, embodied artificial intelligence. Formalizing this capacity in naturalistic, embodied settings has been a longstanding challenge. Here, we present GenEA, a novel agent representation capable of reasoning over multi-step, long-horizon embodied plans. articles.title: From Egocentric Human Video to Robot Manipulation in the Era of Embodied Intelligence
articles.summary: Egocentric human video (EHV) records close-range hand-object interaction (HOI) and the temporal structure of everyday activities, offering a potentially scalable source of experience for robot manipulation. Using this experience for robot control requires recovering useful supervision without recorded robot actions and accounting for differences in morphology, viewpoint, and action space. We define Ego2Robot learning as the process of learning or adapting robot manipulation policies from EHV, organized into four learning paradigms: explicit embodiment transfer, explicit action and task supervision, egocentric video representation pretraining, and latent action and dynamics modeling. The four paradigms differ in what they derive from human video: robot-format demonstrations, interpretable supervision, visual representations, or predictive models of actions and dynamics. articles.summary:
## “艾莫,能助”
艾莫这个名字是7月定下来的,它是怎么来的?
施晓鑫:跟一个短语有关,AI Motion,AI加上运动智能。后来叫着叫着,更被大家理解和引申的是AI加上more——AI延展到物理世界,甚至更多的可能性。
我们内部聊天时还把它引申成“爱莫能助”的谐音:艾莫,能助——它让我们重新思考“小助手”一词的含义——“手”能解决很多问题。
口头流传的时候,我们发现挺朗朗上口,后来便叫了这个名字。命名是个烧脑的过程,既要独特、又能代表我们想表达的含义,可选的好名字并不多。
这四个月你和团队在忙什么?有哪些事是之前没料到的?
施晓鑫:从0到1搭建公司。注册、找场地、完成第一笔融资,整个过程是从学习到熟悉、再到能把控的阶段。没料到的更多是流程和形式上的问题,比如法务。融资对我们来讲是一件熟悉又陌生的事——大家都知道一级市场,也都跟机构聊过,但真正自己去运营一家公司、跟机构打交道,很多事情是新的。公司要展现什么内容给机构?机构在意的是什么?长期要怎么运营和准备?这些都是在企业做职业经理人的时候很少会涉猎的。

施晓鑫:从0到1搭建公司。注册、找场地、完成第一笔融资,整个过程是从学习到熟悉、再到能把控的阶段。没料到的更多是流程和形式上的问题,比如法务。融资对我们来讲是一件熟悉又陌生的事——大家都知道一级市场,也都跟机构聊过,但真正自己去运营一家公司、跟机构打交道,很多事情是新的。公司要展现什么内容给机构?机构在意的是什么?长期要怎么运营和准备?这些都是在企业做职业经理人的时候很少会涉猎的。
## 灵巧手的三道坎
行业里有个说法,人形机器人的竞争终局,一半在手上。你认同吗?
施晓鑫:基本认同。从硬件、本体的角度,手跟身体其余部分的价值可能都相当了,包括操作的价值和难度,可以说一半在手上。
我更倾向于另一种理解:真正发挥价值的一个是手,一个是脑,从这个角度也是一半一半,手和脑应该协同发展。这件事在生物学上也有依据。人的手比猩猩的手灵巧很多,手的进化跟大脑的进化是协同的。脑促进了手的进化,手的灵巧又反过来推动脑的进化。
如果给做灵巧手有难度的影响要素排个优先级——比如自由度、负载、成本、寿命等,你会先解决什么? [...] 从硬件来看,手的成熟度会比本体晚两到三年,衡量的标准就是:能不能有一定规模、能不能以合理的价格获得。目前两只手的成本可能比本体其他部位还贵。
对艾莫来讲,我们会先把基于L2能力的硬件、运动控制、底层的端侧模型(跑在设备本地、不依赖云端的模型)做好、做扎实,未来才有构建L4、L5的基础。如果连遥操作都操作得不好,用手的时候还会故障、还会坏,智能往上走一定会遇到瓶颈。
你预估这个过程会经历多长时间?
施晓鑫 :未来一到两年,基于灵巧操作的操作能力本身会得到很大的发展。要到L4、L5真正形成我们理想中的物理AI和落地场景,需要更长的时间,比如3~5年。
但这3~5年并不是代表一个清晰的界限。它更像是一个阶段,可能在某些场景先发生,做得还不够好,或者只能在这一个场景里做,然后再拓展到十个、一百个、一万个场景。整个过程可能持续更长,这也是我们做好长期投入的准备。

articles.title: ExRL: Sample-Efficient Online Adaptation of Long-Chunk Policies via Execution Length Control
articles.summary: Predicting long action chunks, often spanning dozens of timesteps, has become a key ingredient in increasingly capable robot policies. In this paper, we find that adapting these long-chunk policies with existing reinforcement learning (RL) methods can require many online samples due to the high dimensionality of the action chunks being optimized, making such adaptation impractical in real-world scenarios where interaction data are costly to collect. Our key insight is to shift adaptation from optimizing actions to optimizing how long to execute each predicted action chunk. This keeps the adaptation space low-dimensional while its expressivity grows with the chunk size. We thus introduce Execution at the Right Length (ExRL), a simple approach which augments the base policy with a lightweight adapter that predicts the execution length of each chunk and is trained using off-policy RL algorithms. articles.title: Discrete Model-Based Diffusion for Combinatorial Optimization in Multi-Robot Task Allocation
articles.summary: Decision making in multi-agent and multi-robot systems often involves discrete decision variables, leading to NP-hard combinatorial optimization problems that must be solved within seconds for near real-time implementation. Denoising diffusion has emerged as a powerful tool for such problems, but existing approaches face a trade-off: Model-Based Diffusion (MBD) incorporates diffusion in sampling-based optimization (SBO) without training but only over continuous spaces, while existing diffusion-based combinatorial solvers operate over discrete spaces but require offline training. To this end, we propose Discrete Model-Based Diffusion (Discrete MBD), a training-free SBO method that directly optimizes discrete variables by approximating categorical reverse transition distributions through Monte Carlo sampling. articles.title: AHEADance: Anticipatory Humanoid Dance from Streaming Audio
articles.summary: A humanoid that dances to streamed music must commit each motion chunk before it has heard the music that chunk accompanies, and must continue from motion it has already committed. We present AHEADance, a robot-native streaming dance generator executed on a humanoid robot by a whole-body tracker. ListenAhead conditions each chunk on heard music and a frozen music model's forecasts of the coming music, aligned to their target times and weighted by reliability. The forecasts carry the timing of upcoming beats almost as well as the actual future; with them, the generator is better synchronized with the music and concentrates more motion energy at its song's beat frequency. Commit Forcing trains continuation from the model's own committed chunks, updating both the latent history and the decoded boundary of the next chunk; it reduces low activity from 83.5% to 10.3%, the level of real dance. articles.title: Force-Closure Condition for Cooperative Multi-robot Pushing of Rectangular Objects
articles.summary: In cooperative object manipulation, the placement of pushing contacts determines whether force closure can be achieved and agents can generate arbitrary forces and torques on the object correspondingly. This study derives a necessary and sufficient closed-form condition for the planar force closure of a rectangular object, a common object shape in everyday settings, under four frictionless pushing contacts. For a rectangle of length $b$ and width $a$, force closure holds if and only if $(l_1+l_3-b)(l_2+l_4-a)<0$, where $l_1,l_2,l_3,l_4$ are the four edge contact locations. This condition is independent of the object's center of mass and is used to verify contact configurations before contact force allocation. When the condition is not satisfied, the signs of the two factors indicate which opposing contact pair should be adjusted. articles.title: World In-Context Learning for Agentic Robot Manipulation
articles.summary: Trained action policies write manipulation skill into network weights, tying what is learned to the distribution it is learned from. In-context learning (ICL) avoids this coupling but has not matched trained policies, because a demonstration recorded in another scene carries no feedback from the world the robot currently faces. We observe that what an agent learns in context is semantic, recording task steps and object roles rather than visual appearance, so experience gathered in one world transfers to another. Based on this insight, we propose World In-Context Learning (WICL), a paradigm in which a frozen model starts from a demonstration, rehearses the task in a world such as a simulator, and writes the feedback into its context rather than its weights. We build RoboScript, a modular infrastructure that implements WICL for agentic manipulation. articles.title: Simulating Vein Compressibility for Ultrasound-Guided Femoral Access: Speed, Accuracy, and Phantom Validation
articles.summary: In ultrasound-guided femoral access, probe pressure deforms the tissue and changes the vascular anatomy a robot observes. A simulator must reproduce these mechanics fast enough for robotic interaction, yet the computational effort needed for a clinically meaningful signal like vein collapse before artery is unclear. We test the feasibility of a physics-based simulation in NVIDIA's Isaac Sim for Healthcare, with Stable Neo-Hookean tissue solved by Vertex Block Descent on one GPU. A simulation of a low-fidelity cylindrical benchtop phantom with known geometry and mechanical properties, pressed by a robot, predicted its artery within 5 percentage points at every depth. It matched the vein within 3 points through 11 mm of a 25.4 mm press and followed the collapse behavior of the low-fidelity physical phantom. articles.title: Learning Heterogeneous Tactile Representation for General Dexterous Manipulation
articles.summary: Tactile sensing is an indispensable modality for contact-rich dexterous manipulation, a capability that hints at the ultimate frontiers of embodied intelligence. However, commercially available tactile sensors are still at a relatively early stage of development, with each type of sensor offering irreplaceable strengths alongside its own drawbacks. A key challenge is thus to free tactile understanding from sensor-specific physics, so that embodied models can effectively leverage heterogeneous tactile data. To this end, we develop LingBot-Touch, a tactile foundation model characterized by the following properties. (i) Our model yields a unified representation across different tactile sensors (i.e., piezoresistive, magnetic, and visuotactile sensors), and is easily extensible to new sensor types. articles.title: Benchmarking Real-World Robotic Manipulation through Stochastic Challenges
articles.summary: A challenging bottleneck in manipulation research is reproducibility and comparability of methods in real-world environments. Since manipulation is an interactive task, it cannot be evaluated on a static dataset of observations. Benchmarking in simulation is a common remedy, but cannot cover the whole complexity of real-world tests. This paper proposes a new paradigm of stochastic challenges. Like the well-known YCB objects, it is based on reproducible real-world scenes and therefore allows system-level innovation and comparability between different platforms. Due to their stochastic nature, our challenges however, mimic the rigor and surprise of hidden test sets. To this end, we show how different robots in different labs can be compared based on their success rate over different random task samples, if these samples come from the same distribution. articles.summary: World models have increasingly been applied as a model-based control method for robotics tasks such as manipulation and locomotion. While early world model architectures relied on decoders to prevent mode collapse and learn a predictable latent space, recent works on world models, such as Joint Embedding Predictive Architecture or LeWorldModel, increasingly aim to learn embeddings without a grounding decoder, utilising only a latent forward dynamics predictor and a stabilising entropy term. articles.summary: Vision-language-action (VLA) models are trained as general-purpose foundation models for robot learning, and require fine-tuning for each downstream task and robot. This raises practical questions such as how much data and training updates are needed, how checkpoints should be selected, and whether simulation can be leveraged to alleviate the cost of real data collection. We study these questions on a task that requires both precise manipulation and spatial understanding of the scene. articles.title: Simulation-aided Reinforcement Learning with Control Variates
articles.summary: Reinforcement Learning (RL) algorithms often rely on data collected from a target environment, which can be expensive and noisy. Although simulators can generate large amounts of additional data, standard simulation mixing approaches, which directly combine simulated and real experience, can degrade performance due to simulator inaccuracies, especially when they bias the solution away from the optimal policy. We propose a conservative simulation-aided learning method based on control variates, where simulated data is used solely to reduce variance in the learning process rather than directly shaping the learning target. We develop our approach for Policy-Evaluation, which is a fundamental building block of RL algorithms. ## 人形机器人和家用机器人:令人兴奋,但仍需要时间
AI方面的进展,也把我们带到了大家最兴奋的话题:人形机器人和具身机器人。
现在,全球范围内都有大量资金投入人形机器人研发,中国也是一样。这显然是机器人下一步重要的发展方向之一。但从时间上看,不同人的判断非常不同。
有些人认为一两年内就能够实现大规模具身智能落地,也有人认为永远不可能实现。
绝大多数人的判断处于两者之间。我的看法是:我们相信可以实现,但需要时间。就像协作机器人一样,它也需要一定时间才能被市场接受、被企业部署、被应用场景验证。
为什么我们要做人形机器人?因为如果这种机器人真正成熟,它可以应用在各个领域,可以帮助人类,也可以成为服务机器人,并在人类环境中工作。最近,我们也看到有公司已经在美国公开上市,成为首家上市的人形机器人制造商。
与此同时,在消费者领域,近年来美国也有公司发布面向消费者的人形机器人产品。我们认为,人形机器人最终是一种工具。它们会和人一起合作,在有人环境中长期工作。

articles.title: Bridging Task Planning and Execution for Language-Conditioned Bimanual Manipulation
articles.summary: Robots are increasingly expected to execute natural-language manipulation tasks in real-world environments. This is particularly relevant in household assistance and logistics, where clutter requires reasoning about both task objectives and execution feasibility. This challenge becomes even more pronounced for bimanual humanoid platforms, where coordinating two manipulators introduces additional interaction and kinematic constraints. We present a zero-shot vision-language framework for execution-aware bimanual manipulation that jointly reasons about task objectives and physical feasibility. Planning is grounded in a structured scene representation that combines semantic object relations with execution constraints, enabling the selection of obstacle relocations and execution choices while preserving task semantics. Compatible actions are organised into parallel bimanual stages with explicit pre- and post-conditions. A hierarchical validator evaluates these conditions under perceptual un

articles.title: PCTac: Mechanochromic Photonic-Crystal Tactile Sensor for Dexterous Manipulation
articles.summary: Modern visuotactile sensors primarily sense contact by imaging the deformation of a compliant interface. Using techniques such as photometric stereo, they can recover detailed contact geometry, often represented as surface normals or depth. However, force-related information typically still needs to be inferred indirectly through calibration, geometric reconstruction, or learned mappings. Mechanochromic photonic-crystal (PC) materials offer an alternative physical encoding mechanism: contact loading changes their periodic microstructure and spectral response, directly transforming local stress into a spatially resolved structural-color field. Despite this potential, PC materials have rarely been explored as visuotactile sensors for closed-loop robot learning. We present PCTac, an open-source mechanochromic PC fingertip that uses a dense hue field as its tactile observation. articles.title: Safety-Constrained Intelligent Control of a 2-DOF Robotic Manipulator Using Control Barrier Functions
articles.summary: Control barrier function (CBF) filters depend on dynamic models that can be inaccurate when their parameters and external forces are uncertain. This paper investigates a radial basis function (RBF) neural network compensator whose output is shared by a Cartesian tracking controller and a joint-space CBF filter. An auxiliary state driven by the difference between requested and applied torques corrects the learning signal, reducing the direct influence of filter intervention on adaptation. A two-link manipulator is evaluated through constrained regulation, ablations, matched uncertainty and disturbance trials, and operating-range and timing studies. The results demonstrate that the proposed controller improves tracking while maintaining joint, velocity, and torque limits under parameter uncertainty, and that both the shared compensation and the auxiliary correction contribute to this improvement.

articles.title: VLA-MOPD: On-Policy Distillation for Multi-Task VLA Policy Consolidation
articles.summary: Physical intelligence requires embodied agents to ground language in observations and execute actions while retaining useful skills. Vision-language-action (VLA) policies offer a shared interface, but task-specific post-training often produces separate specialists. Consolidation is difficult: mixed-task reinforcement learning provides sparse trajectory-level credit, while offline distillation may miss student-visited observations and endpoint distillation does not supervise intermediate action-generation states. We introduce VLA Multi-teacher On-Policy Distillation (VLA-MOPD), a protocol for consolidating flow-matching VLA specialists. After acquiring task or suite experts, a shared student collects robot rollouts and queries the instruction-routed frozen teacher at each visited observation and intermediate ordinary differential equation (ODE) state. articles.title: Robo-MLT: Dual-System Robotic Manipulation for Long-Horizon Medical Laboratory Tasks
articles.summary: Reliable medical laboratory automation requires robots to complete entire workflows in protocol order while handling changes during execution. A robot may execute each motion correctly yet fail the workflow by confusing visually similar stages or stalling after human intervention. We present Robo-MLT, a dual-system framework that couples explicit workflow monitoring with learned action generation. A vision--language planner composes an ordered atomic-skill sequence from the protocol and the initial workspace observation. A multiframe execution monitor detects when the active skill has completed or become infeasible, then advances the workflow or triggers replanning. A skill-conditioned vision--language--action policy generates the manipulation trajectories, and an asynchronous runtime coordinates it with the monitor. We evaluate Robo-MLT against four policy baselines and a VLM-based monitor baseline on blood gas analysis and blood sample tube sorting, with 50 nominal configurations per

articles.title: Embodied First Exam
articles.summary: Early successes on agentic robotics point to a potential paradigm shift toward using coding agents to control robots. Existing robotics benchmarks are built around visuomotor policy learning, leaving it open whether coding agents can reliably control diverse robots under physical-world constraints. We therefore introduce the Embodied First Exam, a unified, comprehensive, and agent-native evaluation framework where coding agents can choose their own control approach: direct control, code to control, or train a policy to control. We hope it serves as a first exam for coding agents before they enter the physical world, with 1,156 tasks in 35 suites on 47 robots, including 9 new suites that go beyond pick-and-place to spatial puzzles, dexterous manipulation, multi-robot interaction, dynamic whole-body control, and sim-to-sim engineering. Each task can be run in up to three evaluation settings. The Standard Setting mimics the real world: the agent receives only sensor observations and, by d

articles.title: GeoMind: A Benchmark for Spatial Understanding in Robotic Manipulation
articles.summary: Robotic manipulation has advanced rapidly in mapping visual observations and language instructions to actions. However, reliable manipulation in open-world environments requires robust spatial understanding: the ability to identify targets in complex layouts (spatial reasoning) and adapt to scenes that continuously evolve through interaction (spatial memory). Yet existing embodied benchmarks fall short in evaluating spatial understanding: they often introduce strong visual cues that bypass spatial reasoning, and focus on static scenes that offer little insight into an agent's capacity for spatial memory. To address this gap, we introduce GeoMind, a systematic benchmark for structured spatial understanding through tabletop manipulation. GeoMind comprises 54 evaluated task variants organized around spatial reasoning and spatial memory. It also incorporates a scalable pipeline that automates the generation and annotation of task instances with verified targets and executable interactions.

articles.title: LHNav: Long-Horizon Humanoid Navigation via Multirate Coordination and Physics-Grounded Action Data
articles.summary: We study humanoid navigation across multiple destinations under long-horizon language instructions. This task is challenging because robots must maintain progress across successive goals while continuously producing natural, stable whole-body motion through confined spaces. However, task decomposition in existing methods does not by itself ensure progress throughout execution, while waypoint-based navigation does not guarantee natural, route-faithful whole-body motion. Our key idea is to organize navigation into three complementary roles operating at different time scales: a Brain for task reasoning, a Cerebellum for local motion generation, and a Brainstem for whole-body execution. We realize this idea in LHNav, an asynchronous system that uses progress and arrival feedback to coordinate navigation goals, VLA motion-token prediction, and whole-body control. articles.title: GAP: Generalized Adaptation Prior for Dexterous Piano Playing
articles.summary: Dexterous hands enable versatile manipulation, but policies trained in simulation often degrade on hardware owing to non-idealities, and the high-dimensional action space makes real-world adaptation costly. Piano playing, which requires precise and coordinated multifinger motion, offers a representative testbed. We propose GAP (Generalized Adaptation Prior for Dexterous Piano Playing), a sample-efficient adaptation framework that learns how to adapt, rather than how to act, during simulation pretraining and transfers this adaptation prior to hardware. Between repeated executions, GAP uses feedback to adjust the actions of the next one: a gradient guidance network learns from paired executions how adjusting actions affects playing performance, and its gradients guide these adjustments. In simulation, GAP yields approximately 2.4 times the F1 scores improvement of the existing fast-adaptation baseline for dexterous piano playing under the same interaction budget. articles.title: SPARK: Simple Post-training for Adapting pRetrained Knowledge to Robot Control
articles.summary: Large-scale representation learning has produced public foundation models that provide strong general-purpose visual features. However, their pretraining objectives are not designed for robot representation learning, so the resulting embeddings tend to emphasize global semantics rather than the temporally sensitive representations required for robot control. Training robot models from scratch is also undesirable due to the limited scale and high collection cost of robotics data, as well as the substantial computational burden of pre-training. In this paper, we propose SPARK (Simple Post-training for Adapting pRetrained Knowledge), a post-training method that adapts foundation models to robot control. articles.title: Compass 1: Towards Open-World and Persistent Embodied Navigation from Monocular RGB Videos
articles.summary: Embodied navigation requires agents to achieve persistent spatial awareness and long-horizon execution stability in open-world environments. However, existing navigation architectures struggle to sustain both capabilities, remaining effective only over a handful of recent frames. We present Compass 1, the first embodied navigation foundation model to unify language understanding and video generation while enabling memory backtracking through nearly 2mins of visual history. Without altering the underlying architecture, we introduce History Representation, which integrates sparse visual keyframes with an explicit History Representation Map to preserve long-term spatiotemporal context. To effectively leverage this history, we further introduce History Utilization, a structured VQA supervision protocol comprising three categories: task-stage grounding, exploration consistency, and spatiotemporal target retrieval, enabling map-grounded reasoning and stable persistent long-horizon navigation

articles.title: OASIS: Optimization-Aware Subgoal Inference with Safety Constraints for Autonomous Mobile Robot Navigation
articles.summary: Navigation in dynamic environments requires mobile robots to make progress toward their goals while respecting motion limits and avoiding surrounding obstacles. Learned subgoal policies can guide model predictive control beyond its local prediction horizon, but a geometrically suitable subgoal does not necessarily lead to a successfully solved control problem. This paper proposes OASIS, a hierarchical navigation framework that incorporates recent optimization outcomes into reinforcement learning-based subgoal generation. A high-level policy trained using Soft Actor--Critic generates local subgoals, while a nonlinear model predictive controller tracks them subject to motion limits, geometric collision-avoidance constraints, and embedded high-order control barrier function constraints. The outcomes of controller optimizations over each subgoal interval are summarized and provided to the policy at its next decision, without requiring additional optimization calls. articles.title: Thermo-VLA: A Thermal-Aware Vision-Language-Action Model with Gated Residual Modulation for Robotic Manipulation
articles.summary: Recent Vision-Language-Action (VLA) models have begun incorporating thermal sensing, but existing approaches typically treat thermal images as ordinary visual inputs, providing limited support for temperature-aware relational reasoning in manipulation. To address this limitation, we propose Thermo-VLA with a ThermoRes Encoder, which decomposes thermal images into cold and hot attribute representations and injects them into the RGB token through language-conditioned residual modulation, enabling temperature-driven target selection and continuous manipulation. We further construct six real-world robotic tasks on a dual-arm Unitree G1 platform, spanning basic grounding to relational reasoning. Experiments show that Thermo-VLA achieves an average success rate of 0.86 across four thermal-dependent tasks, outperforming a pi_0.5 baseline that directly incorporates RGB-thermal observations by 18 percentage points. articles.title: Flip Anything with Agentic Robotics Self-Learning
articles.summary: Flipping is a fundamental robotic manipulation skill that requires reorienting a target object in a stable pose on a planar support surface by rotating it 180$^\circ$ about an axis parallel to the support surface -- think of flipping a coin from heads to tails. Although flipping is a common objective in industrial tasks such as parts inspection, mechanical assembly, and tool use, coding a bimanual robot with grippers to flip diverse objects is a significant challenge. In this paper, we show that a coding agent can autonomously develop and refine object-flipping strategies through iterative learning in physics simulations across diverse object geometries. Progressive skill acquisition, from basic handover to toppling and pushing, robust grasping and sensing, and thin-object manipulation with recovery, improves task success from 24.7% to 95.0%. The resulting graph-based code integrates high-level strategy selection with reactive control, enabling multi-stage flipping on physical robots.

articles.title: Fade to... Red? Scheduling Coloured Noise Exploration Supports Efficient Robot Learning with Reduced Movement Jerk
articles.summary: Exploration in deep reinforcement learning (RL) for continuous control is commonly driven by temporally uncorrelated Gaussian (white) action noise, which leads to jerky motions with locally constrained exploration. In contrast, temporally correlated coloured noise, particularly pink noise, has been shown to support more efficient exploration in RL. Motivated by these findings, we inquire whether scheduling changes to the noise colour over the course of training can outperform white noise for continuous control robotics. We perform a systematic study of 49 linear schedules between white and red noise, together with generalised state-dependent exploration (gSDE), on four sparse-reward manipulation tasks with a Fetch arm and a Shadow Dexterous Hand. We find that the noise colour at the end of training does not affect learning efficiency or end performance, whereas fading towards red noise halves the jerk of exploration in every task. articles.summary: Vision-language-action (VLA) models pair a vision-language backbone with an action head, but in closed-loop control the backbone sits on the control-critical path: while it computes, the robot keeps moving, so each executed action is conditioned on an increasingly stale observation. A larger backbone therefore directly blocks reactivity, especially in humanoid dexterous manipulation. We present DASH, a Decoupled Asynchronous System for Humanoids that removes this coupling. DASH splits the policy into a slow vision-language model (System 2) and a fast flow-matching action head (System 1) that run as concurrent processes over the LCM communication protocol, so the control rate is set by the action head alone, independent of backbone size. articles.title: PAIR: Proprioception-Aligned Image-Ray Representations for Viewpoint-Robust Manipulation
articles.summary: While imitation learning has made substantial progress toward generalizable robot manipulation through scaling, viewpoint robustness remains a major bottleneck. Visuomotor policies rely heavily on visual inputs, yet images provide an inherently ambiguous signal under viewpoint change: similar scenes may appear markedly different across viewpoints, while distinct states may share certain visual overlaps. A policy must therefore infer not only the task-relevant state, but also how it is visually projected under a particular camera configuration. This entanglement of viewpoint-dependent appearance and task-relevant state can make learning inefficient and limit generalization to unseen viewpoints. Recent work has begun to address this challenge through camera-ray conditioning and representation learning using geometric cues to induce invariance. articles.title: Particle Filtering with Generative Trajectory Models for State Estimation and Control
articles.summary: Generative models can support both state estimation and control in robotics. For control, a common approach is to use the model as a policy that directly samples actions conditioned on observation histories. However, models that jointly represent states, actions, and observations can also predict how the robot state and its environment evolve. We investigate whether these predictions can improve state estimation and control through a change in inference procedure, without modifying the pretrained model. To this end, we use particle filtering to maintain competing hypotheses about state histories. A single pretrained diffusion model generates these hypotheses along with their predicted observations and associated action proposals. As new measurements arrive, particles are reweighted according to how well their predicted observations match the measurements. articles.title: Accelerated Reinforcement Learning for Soft Robotics: Hours Instead of Years
articles.summary: Reinforcement learning (RL) requires large amounts of interaction data or a reliable simulator, both hard to obtain for nonlinear soft robotic hardware. We demonstrate that an aSSM-reduced model, a simple polynomial ordinary differential equation learned purely from pre-collected data, can serve as an RL training environment. articles.title: Data-Driven Precision Control of Soft Helicoid Robots
articles.summary: A purely data-driven method grounded in the theory of adiabatic spectral submanifolds (aSSMs) was recently used to model and control nonlinear soft robotic simulators. Specifically, we learn a five dimensional (5D) aSSM-reduced nonlinear ordinary differential equation (ODE) that accurately models the dynamics of a soft-helicoid trunk robot. We then use this ODE in a model predictive control scheme to demonstrate real-time precision control across various challenging closed-loop trajectory-tracking tasks, ranging from 2D to 3D trajectories with static and dynamic constraints. We find that our methodology enhances accuracy and precision across all control tasks compared to available data-driven linear methods and model-free reinforcement learning. articles.summary: Robot policies increasingly act through a small vocabulary of discrete latent actions learned from unlabeled video, yet training leaves open which motion receives which code. We find this choice highly unstable: two independently trained runs of Moto's latent motion tokenizer assign the same robot clips to nearly unrelated codes (adjusted Rand index 0.001), and evaluating one tokenizer in bf16 instead of fp32 reassigns 74% of its tokens. articles.summary: Humanoid robots have achieved significant progress in locomotion and manipulation, enabling traversal over rough terrain and richer interaction with the environment, such as moving obstacles. However, most traditional navigation methods assume non-interactive environments and focus only on traversal. These limitations become critical in outdoor rough-terrain scenarios, where robots must jointly reason about terrain traversability and object movability. articles.summary: Frequent heavy lifting is linked to musculoskeletal strain, with lower back pain affecting up to 40% of manual labourers. Inspired by animals using tails for balance, we developed a wearable robotic tail as a dynamic counterbalance. Ten participants performed an imitated shelf loading/unloading task across three conditions: active tail, passive tail, and no tail. articles.title: FlowEval: How Much Adaptation Does an Embodied Foundation Model Need at Deployment?
articles.summary: Large-scale pretraining is reducing the amount of adaptation required to deploy embodied foundation models, but it is not guaranteed that a pretrained model already provide the level of performance required in every deployment. We study whether a small set of successful target-domain demonstrations can reveal whether and how much target-domain data will be required before any adaptation. articles.title: Kimodo-Policy: Learning Kinematic Action Models for Humanoid Loco-Manipulation
articles.summary: Humanoid loco-manipulation requires continuous coordination of high-dimensional whole-body motion to realize task objectives. articles.title: Review the Episodes, Refine the Lessons: Simple Memory Evolution for Embodied Agents
articles.summary: Recent studies of embodied agents based on frontier multimodal large language models (MLLMs) develop harness engineering around the MLLM, such as harnesses with post-trained policies and recursive self-improvement loops. articles.title: 短期降温不改长期趋势,具身智能投资更看重赛道前景与企业成长潜力-36氪
articles.summary:
### 行业热度:融资金额回落,资金更关注可验证的经营进展
融资降温尚不等于资金全面退出,需求明确、经营进展可验证的项目更有说服力。第一财经据IT桔子事件库梳理,7—9月披露融资额分别为86.54亿元、175.41亿元和71.50亿元,9月较8月下降59.2%;地瓜机器人、苏度科技等仍获十亿元级融资。该报季后采访也显示,部分机构更关注真实订单与现金可支撑时长。
### 政策驱动:政策支持延续,地方布局更强调产业适配与使用成效
政策支持延续,地方布局更强调产业适配、真实需求与使用成效。8月28日,国家发展改革委既支持实训场、中试基地及数据、模型、标准建设,也强调围绕真实场景、真实需求推进应用。9月国家数据局座谈会延续这一方向。支持创新与约束盲目投入并行,地方不仅要比较招商数量和建设规模,更需说明本地有什么客户、配套与运营条件。
### 技术驱动:陌生环境作业能力改善,可靠性与经济性决定落地速度 [...] 融资降温与应用扩展在同一季度发生。9月披露融资额低于7月和8月,但仍有十亿元级融资;9月10日,国家数据局继续支持企业增加数据投入,强调科学布局。9月24日,智元与长隆宣布首期部署超过300台机器人,覆盖演艺、导览等场景。资本趋于审慎,应用探索并未停止。局部投入和估值过热的风险值得警惕,仍须逐项检验交易、使用成效与回报条件。
## 二、六维证据指向短期调整,真实需求与技术进步仍支撑长期发展
综合研判:短期调整预期与投入节奏,长期机会取决于需求兑现和企业能力
六维证据支持“短期降温不改长期趋势”:资本与政策要求投入更加审慎,技术、销售和应用又提供了持续发展的依据。当前更接近预期、交易质量与投入节奏的阶段性校正,尚不足以据此判断产业需求全面收缩;调整持续多久,仍取决于后续技术和经营进展。
长期增长也不会平均分配给所有赛道和企业。需求强度、技术门槛、成本收益与竞争结构决定赛道空间;产品复用、稳定交付和客户经营决定企业能否获得增长;交易价格则决定增长能否转化为投资回报。
以下从行业热度、政策驱动、技术驱动、市场规模、客户需求与商业化进程六个维度,分别说明上述判断的证据与边界。

articles.title: On Agentic Manipulation Policies
articles.summary: Recent work on robot manipulation has focused on specialist policies trained on demonstrations. We show that generalist AI models can control manipulators more reliably than specialist policies such as vision-language-action models (VLAs) and world-action models (WAMs). We systematically analyze agentic manipulation policies (AMPs), in which a generalist AI model commands the manipulator directly, adapting its actions as the task unfolds. We present AMP1, a reference harness that runs unchanged across single-arm, bimanual, and mobile manipulation. AMP1 achieves state-of-the-art results on the RoboLab-120 and CaP-Gym benchmarks, with no demonstrations or task-specific training. On RoboLab-120, AMP1 reaches an 85.6\% success rate zero-shot, compared to 49.2\% and 42.9\% for leading VLA and WAM policies. The agent succeeds zero-shot in 104 of 108 real-world trials spanning twelve tasks and three robot instances, reducing failure rates by 20x and 15x relative to strong VLA and WAM baseline

articles.title: Grasp-TAGS: Task-Aware Grasp Selection via Critic Distillation for Prehensile Loco-Manipulation
articles.summary: Loco-manipulation, which requires mobile manipulators to coordinate locomotion and manipulation over long horizons, is a key capability for large-object rearrangement in applications such as service robotics and warehouse automation. Despite recent progress, reliably executing these tasks remains challenging because performance depends on complex robot-object and object-environment interaction dynamics. Existing approaches address this challenge either through model-based methods, which often require accurate dynamics models, or through learning-based methods, which reduce this requirement but typically assume a fixed or predefined initial grasp. However, different geometrically stable grasps can lead to substantially different downstream manipulation performance. Therefore, we propose Grasp-TAGS, a task-aware grasp selection framework for goal-conditioned large-object rearrangement. We train a unified PPO-based reinforcement learning policy across multiple initial grasp configurations

articles.title: Computer-Use Agents Are Embodied Generalists
articles.summary: In many areas of AI, general-purpose models have increasingly replaced handcrafted methods and specialized architectures. We argue that embodied AI is poised for a similar shift. Our key claim is that embodied tasks can be formulated as interaction with digital software. Specifically, we build software that renders an agent's view of a physical environment on a screen and provides controls for acting in it. A computer-use agent (CUA) can then perform embodied tasks through the same screenshots and keyboard and mouse actions that it uses to operate ordinary software. Using a single CUA design and changing only the software, our entries win first-, second-, third-, and sixth-place prizes across four ECCV workshop competitions, without any competition-specific agent tuning. articles.title: Seeing What Matters: Benchmarking Task-Conditioned Actionable Spatial Belief for Manipulation
articles.summary: When should a robot look at the cup, and when at the portafilter? Spatial-reasoning benchmarks evaluate whether a model can describe a scene, but manipulation needs something more specific: the ability to acquire the particular evidence that makes the current command executable. A view that is informative for one task can be useless for another, even at the same workstation. We introduce Seeing What Matters, a benchmark for task-conditioned actionable spatial belief in simulated tabletop manipulation. Across three domains--coffee workstation, drawer/cabinet, and microwave/appliance--the benchmark provides 860 frozen evaluation cases; expanding across methods, budgets, and inference repeats yields more than 115,000 evaluator episodes under two protocols: closed-loop actionability and same-object functional out-of-distribution generalization. articles.title: SURE:Spatiotemporal Uncertainty Representation for Efficient Vision-Language-Action Learning
articles.summary: Vision-language-action (VLA) policies have become a promising paradigm for end-to-end robot control, but their effectiveness still depends heavily on large volumes of demonstration data. In manipulation tasks, this dependence is compounded by structured spatiotemporal uncertainty in the action space: multiple nearby actions or trajectories may successfully solve the same task, while semantically equivalent demonstrations often unfold at different speeds. Standard pointwise supervision treats each demonstrated action as an exact target, imposing an unnecessary learning burden under such uncertainty. We present SURE, a data-efficient VLA training framework that explicitly models both spatial and temporal uncertainty. SURE augments a VLA backbone with a lightweight transposed-convolutional probabilistic action decoder that captures spatial uncertainty through local correlations among neighboring action bins. It further introduces Soft-DTW alignment supervision to accommodate local timing

articles.title: ODEAction: From Predicting Chunks to Evolving Actions
articles.summary: Vision-language-action (VLA) models typically generate actions in chunks, organizing continuous robot execution into separately predicted segments and thus introducing potential discontinuities at action-chunk transitions. We propose ODEAction, a chunk-free action generation paradigm that replaces action-chunk prediction with Continuous Action Evolution. Given visual observations, language instructions, and robot proprioceptive information, ODEAction learns an action transition field defined over action space, where a transition vector characterizes the evolution rate of the current action with respect to evolution time. During execution, the model takes the current action as its initial condition and integrates the learned field using an ordinary differential equation (ODE), recursively generating subsequent actions with explicit dependencies. articles.title: DKWBC: Decoupling Motion Tracking and Balancing for Humanoid Whole-Body Control
articles.summary: Humanoid whole-body control requires a robot to track diverse reference motions while maintaining balance under gravity, torque limits, contact switching, and external disturbances. Existing reinforcement-learning-based trackers typically learn control outputs that jointly address motion tracking and balance. However, similar reference poses can correspond to substantially different dynamic demands, requiring a unified policy to learn motion-dependent control requirements alongside balance corrections. This can complicate learning and lead to high-frequency fluctuations in control outputs. We propose DKWBC, a dynamics-informed whole-body control framework that combines explicit model-based tracking with a learned balancing residual. Horizon-Coupled Obstacle Guidance for Relative-Action Diffusion Policies
articles.summary: Real-world robot deployment requires adapting learned policies to unseen obstacles without collecting new demonstrations or retraining. Existing policy-level guidance often applies obstacle corrections independently at individual horizon steps, which may address local obstacle violations but fail to coordinate the action sequence into a complete, task-directed detour. How obstacle responses should be propagated across the action horizon to coordinate complete, task-directed avoidance motion remains underexplored. We introduce an inferencetime obstacle-guidance framework for pretrained relative-action diffusion policies. It rolls out cumulative relative actions into a workspace trajectory, evaluates obstacle interactions along the trajectory with an SDF-based obstacle model, and propagates each obstacle response to all contributing action increments during denoising. articles.title: MDF++: Visuo-Tactile World Action Model with End-to-end Representation Learning
articles.summary: Recently, world-action models (WAMs) have emerged as a powerful framework for robot manipulation. By jointly modeling action generation and future observation prediction, WAMs can act and anticipate the outcomes of the actions. However, existing WAMs typically rely on frozen pretrained encoders trained with reconstruction, which may not produce representations well suited for robot control. In this paper, we tackle the problem of learning physicallygrounded, control-relevant representations for WAMs. We propose MDF++, a visuo-tactile world-action model that learns latent representations of multisensory observations end-to-end with a diffusion backbone. While naive joint training can lead to feature collapse, MDF++ introduces a multi-task learning strategy that leverages cross-modal correlations to learn task-relevant representations. articles.title: SUGARv2: Learning Diverse Visual Humanoid Loco-Manipulation Skills from Synthesized Interaction References
articles.summary: Scaling up visual humanoid loco-manipulation skill acquisition requires reducing the human effort needed as tasks and spatial configurations expand, particularly in demonstration collection and task-specific training design. We present SUGARv2, a unified framework for learning diverse visual humanoid loco-manipulation skills through interaction reference synthesis and a shared training pipeline. To obtain diverse references at low cost, we adapt reusable task templates to different spatial configurations, synthesizing coordinated robot and object motions. To reduce task-specific reward design and training effort, we use reference-based imitation as a common learning objective across tasks. articles.title: Augmentron: Scalable Multi-View Visual Augmentation for Robot Learning
articles.summary: Robot policies trained on visually narrow demonstrations can become sensitive to environmental features that are unrelated to the task. Existing generative augmentation methods can introduce visual diversity, but processing every frame and camera view independently is computationally expensive and may produce inconsistent observations across cameras and timestamps. We introduce Augmentron, a geometry-aware pipeline that generates reusable scene representations and renders them through recorded camera poses. This produces temporally and multi-view consistent environ- ment and workspace variations while preserving the robot, task objects, actions, and annotations. Across three physical manipulation tasks, replacing half of the real world training dataset with Augmentron data improves model success across three tasks for both in out-of-distribution distractor objects, and out-of-distribution workspace variation evaluations. articles.title: Toward the Era of Agentic Embodied Intelligence
articles.summary: Foundation models increasingly guide robot actions, yet sustained autonomy requires efficient control and failure recovery. We introduce A2-MEAS, an embodied multi-agent framework built around code as a scaling interface. Learned correction codes combine corrective language, spatial evidence, execution history, and action proposals. MetaBrain provides training supervision and runtime guidance. A correction encoder and adapter absorb this knowledge into policy weights during training, while fresh codes adapt behavior with frozen weights at deployment. The action model, A2-WLA, adds motion-aware history and a latent world model to a vision-language-action policy. Surprisingly, this simple design with action pretraining and task specialization reaches 0.5755 Q-score on the 50-task BEHAVIOR 2026 public subset before online correction, 2.21x the 2025 winner's reported 0.2605 across different benchmark editions and training configurations. articles.title: DobotTrack: Target-Grounded Vision-Language-Action Learning for Embodied Person Tracking
articles.summary: Language-guided embodied person tracking requires a mobile agent to identify a target from a referring description and consistently follow the target under egocentric observations. We present DobotTrack, a target-grounded vision-language-action (VLA) framework that integrates auxiliary grounding supervision with efficient temporal modeling. We systematically investigate five auxiliary tasks---person segmentation, bounding-box grounding, visual-spatial classification (VSC), future DINO feature prediction, and future-frame prediction---and adopt complementary mask and bounding-box supervision to enhance target delineation and localization. We introduce Q-identity, a target-conditioned historical visual compression module that leverages target-grounding predictions to selectively preserve identity-discriminative appearance features and spatial cues in compact historical tokens. articles.title: ToolDex: An Ego-Exo Human Demonstration Dataset for Creative Physical Tool Use
articles.summary:
Creative tool use is a fundamental human capability and an important step toward general-purpose embodied intelligence. It requires agents to reason about object affordances, physical constraints, and manipulation strategies, especially when standard tools are unavailable. However, progress in this area is limited by the lack of real-world datasets that capture human tool-use behavior with sufficient scale, fidelity, and diversity. Existing benchmarks are often simulation-based, focus on simplified interactions, or lack detailed observations and annotations.
 We introduce ToolDex, a large-scale egocentric-exocentric (ego-exo) human demonstration dataset for creative physical tool use. ToolDex captures scenarios in which humans select, adapt, and repurpose available objects as tools. articles.title: A Controlled Study of Models, Skills, Feedback, and Curriculum in Agentic Robotics
articles.summary: Agentic robotics asks coding agents to implement and iteratively improve robot policies from simulated and real-world physical interactions. We study the self-learning loop of agentic robotics through a controlled simulation study spanning nine manipulation tasks, 631 different experiment configurations, and 28K coding agent rollouts, systematically varying model capability, skill priors, feedback structure, and curriculum. The experiment data suggests that the bottleneck is often not the access to sufficient information, but interpreting it into the right policy update. Across these factors, a successful self-learning loop depends on how effectively agents attribute failures, reason task-relevant spatial and geometric structure, and selectively restructure code to improve policies.

articles.title: FASTFUNNELS: Agile Multi Robot Navigation in Narrow Spaces via Adaptive Dynamic Funnels
articles.summary: We focus on the problem of high-speed multi-robot navigation in cluttered spaces with tight spatial constraints. A key challenge is balancing safety with agility, as existing methods often trade one for the other (slowing down near a bottleneck to avoid collisions versus failing to swerve in time at high speeds), especially for car-like systems. Our approach belongs to the family of formation control methods, in which Ackermann-steering agents coordinate while navigating tight spaces. However, current formation control techniques rely on rigid, pre-defined shapes and transitions that depend on initial conditions, the environment, and vehicle dynamics, and are impractical to maintain at high speeds. For example, agents passing through a small gap must first form a square, transform into a line using analytical equations, and then return to a square. articles.title: RevoSim: Scalable Multimodal Tactile Simulation for Dexterous Manipulation
articles.summary: We present RevoSim, a scalable and high-fidelity multimodal tactile simulator for the BrainCo Revo3 hand that jointly models 285 piezoresistive taxels and five visuotactile fingertips. RevoSim efficiently generates synchronized pressure, depth, RGB, and marker-displacement observations; on a single RTX 5090, its depth-conditioned marker-displacement configuration supports up to 4,096 parallel environments. We train in-hand manipulation and grasping policies entirely in simulation, establishing a foundation for future sim-to-real transfer. Project page: https://braincotech.github.io/RevoSim-web/.

articles.title: HOC2R: Hand-Object Contact Trajectories for Human-to-Robot Motion Transfer
articles.summary: Human videos contain abundant object-manipulation demonstrations, but they do not directly provide motion cues that a robot can follow. We present HOC2R, a Hand-Object Contact trajectory extractor for Robot motion that combines frozen DINOv3 and SAM 2.1 features with learned heads for hand-object association and contact localization. HOC2R supports two modes: count-aware automation that detects, counts, and localizes visible contacts in untrimmed videos, and fixed-two localization for two-finger grippers when contact frames are known. On a 30-task point-annotated benchmark, count-aware automation improves contact-count accuracy from 58.1% to 71.4% and reduces mean localization distance from 19.81 to 10.46 pixels relative to an adapted VRB2 baseline. On seven unseen RGB-D rollouts, a five-task fixed-two checkpoint reduces mean localization distance from 67.67 to 27.02 pixels. articles.title: PRISM: Primitive Routing via In-context Skill Mixing for Retentive VLA Adaptation
articles.summary: Vision-Language-Action (VLA) models promise a single language-conditioned policy adaptable to many manipulation behaviors, yet deployment additionally requires skill retention and long-horizon composition: a policy must retain previously acquired skills and reuse them inside composite tasks whose behavior changes across phases. The standard recipe absorbs every new task into one shared update, which provides neither a parameter-level locus for reusable skills nor a mechanism for invoking each skill along the trajectory.
